html:
The Russian Revolution was the overthrow of the tsar in 1917 and the seizure of power by Lenin's Bolsheviks later that year, which led to the first communist state. It took place in Russia during the First World War.

The war went badly for Russia. Millions of soldiers died, and cities ran short of bread. In February 1917 (March by the Western calendar) strikes and mutinies in Petrograd forced Nicholas II to abdicate. A Provisional Government took over but kept fighting the war, while workers' and soldiers' councils, the soviets, grew in power beside it.

In October 1917 the Bolsheviks under Vladimir Lenin took power in Petrograd. They promised "peace, land and bread", took Russia out of the war in 1918 and nationalised land and industry.

  • A brutal civil war followed, between the Bolshevik Reds and their many enemies. The Reds won by about 1922.
  • The tsar and his family were shot in 1918.
  • War and requisitioning led to the famine of 1921, which killed millions.
  • The Soviet Union was founded at the end of 1922.

After Lenin died in 1924, Joseph Stalin took control. The revolution inspired communist parties across the world and shaped the twentieth century, from China to Cuba, until the Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.
sum: The Russian Revolution was the overthrow of the tsar in 1917 and the seizure of power by Lenin's Bolsheviks later that year, which led to the first communist state. It took place in Russia during the First World War.
